title: AWR/2 BlameAttestation
description: NON-NORMATIVE. JSON Schema is a convenience for tooling and is not the normative definition of AWR/2; awr/SPEC.md is (Appendix B). Where this schema and the specification disagree, the schema is the bug. A BlameAttestation answers which hop failed: attribution of a failure to one node of a multi-step work chain (SPEC.md §3.5).
$comment: This schema checks structure only. It cannot check the one substantive rule of §3.5 — that `blamedWork` is reachable from `chain` through `parents` edges (AWR-BLAME-001) — because that is a graph walk over other documents, nor can it check the digests themselves. See common-v2.json's file-level $comment for the full list of non-expressible requirements, including §4.3's global no-float rule. Never set additionalProperties:false on any object here (§3.1).

type.$comment: SPEC.md §3.1: MUST contain `VerifiableCredential` (AWR-DOC-004) and exactly one AWR type (AWR-DOC-005). Further types MAY be present.

chain.$comment: SPEC.md §3.5: MUST be a digest reference to the receipt of the work whose RESULT was unacceptable — the chain's terminal hop, the observable failure (AWR-BLAME-003). `id` is required here because §3.2 licenses omitting it only for a non-document artefact and this references a receipt; §3.5 does not restate that explicitly, so see the report finding.

blamedWork.$comment: SPEC.md §3.5: MUST be a digest reference to the receipt of the hop held responsible (AWR-BLAME-003). It MAY equal `chain`. It SHOULD be reachable from `chain` through `parents` edges, and a verifier that has the intermediate receipts MUST report AWR-BLAME-001 when it is not — neither the equality nor the reachability is expressible in JSON Schema.

failureClass.$comment: SPEC.md §3.5: MUST be one of these eight (AWR-BLAME-002). `upstream-input` is how a hop is exonerated: the blame is recorded against it while stating that its input was already wrong.

confidence.$comment: SPEC.md §3.5: OPTIONAL, decimal string in [0,1], same rule as `score` (AWR-BLAME-004). MUST NOT be a JSON number (§4.3).

method.$comment: SPEC.md §3.5: MUST be present with a non-empty `id`. §3.5 states no reason code of its own for a missing/empty blame method; AWR-VDCT-003 is registered for the verdict's `method` — see the report finding.

evidence.$comment: SPEC.md §3.5 shows `evidence` with the same shape as §3.4's, so the same definition is used: every entry carries `digestSRI`, `kind` is a free-form label, and the bytes are never fetched (§13.5).
